Short title, extent and commencement

Act No
Act No. XIX of 1948
Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act,
1948.
An Act to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of certain offences punish Able under the Ionian Penal
Code and cer tain other Laws.
PREAMBLE
Whereas it is
expedient to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of
certain offences punishable under the Indian Penal Code and certain other laws;
It is hereby
enacted as follows;
1. Short title, extent and commencement.--- (1) This Act
may be called the Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1948.
(2) It extends to
the whole of Pakistan and applies also to Pakistan subjects, and servants of
the Central or a Provincial Government residing or serving, for the time being, outside
Pakistan, or in any State which has acceded, or may accede to Pakistan, in respect
of offences mentioned in the schedule appended to this Act
or such other offences as may be notified from time to time in the official
gazette in accordance with the provisions of this Act, if committed within, or
in relation to Pakistan.
It shall come into
force at once,

Definition

Act No. XIX of 1948

1948.
An Act to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of certain offences punish Able under the Ionian Penal

certain offences punishable under the Indian Penal Code and certain other laws;
It is hereby
enacted as follows;
2. Definition.-Public servant
for this purposes of this Act, " public servant " means a public
servant as defined in section hl of the Indian Penal Code, Act XLV of 1860 and
also includes every railway employee and every person, who holds any office, or
is otherwise employed by the Central or 'any Provincial Government whether on a
salary or not, for the discharge of any duties in connection with the affairs
of the Central or a Provincial Government.

Appointment of Special Judges

Act No
Act No. XIX of 1948
Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act,
1948.
An Act to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of certain offences punish Able under the Ionian Penal
Code and cer tain other Laws.
PREAMBLE
Whereas it is
expedient to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of
certain offences punishable under the Indian Penal Code and certain other laws;
It is hereby
enacted as follows;
3. Appointment of Special Judges -(1) The Central Government may, for purpose of this
Act, by notification in the official gazette, appoint Special. Judges to try and punish
offences specified in the schedule appended
to this Act and such other offences as may
be notified by from
time to time in the official gazette.
(2) No person
shall be appointed a Special Judge unless he;
(a)
is qualified under sub section 3 of
section 220 of the Government of India Act, 1935, for appointment as Judge of a
High Court ; or
(b) has, for a period of not less than three years exercised,
whether continuously or not, the powers under the Code of Criminal Procedure
Act V of 1898, of a Sessions Judge, Additional Sessions Judge, or a District
Magistrate.

Jurisdiction of Special Judges and cognizance of cases by them

Act No
Act No. XIX of 1948
Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act,
1948.
An Act to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of certain offences punish Able under the Ionian Penal
Code and cer tain other Laws.
PREAMBLE
Whereas it is
expedient to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of
certain offences punishable under the Indian Penal Code and certain other laws;
It is hereby
enacted as follows;
4. Jurisdiction of Special Judges and cognizance of
cases by them.-(1) A Special.
Judge shall have jurisdiction within such territorial limits as may be fixed by
the Central Government by notification in the official gazette in respect of
cases sent up to him for trial by the Special Police Establish ment,
constituted under the Pakistan Special Police Establishment Ordinance, No. VII of 1948.
Provided that for
the purpose of trial before the Special Judge, the provisions of Chapter XVIII of
the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 shall be dispensed with, but a Special
Judge may, in any case where he deems it necessary, order any investigation by
the Special Police Establishment.
(2) The Central
Government may, by order in writing, transfer, any case to the Court of a
Special Judge appionted
under this Act, which relates to any of the offences mentioned in the Schedule
and is pending in any Court, or before the West Punjab Special Tribunal
constituted under the Indian Independence (Special Tribunal) Order, 1947.

Procedure in trial of cases and powers of Special Judges

Act No
Act No. XIX of 1948
Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act,
1948.
An Act to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of certain offences punish Able under the Ionian Penal
Code and cer tain other Laws.
PREAMBLE
Whereas it is
expedient to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of
certain offences punishable under the Indian Penal Code and certain other laws;
It is hereby
enacted as follows;
6.
(1) When any person is charged before a Special Judge with An offence triable under this Act, the fact that such person, or any
other person through him or on his behalf, is in possession, for which he
cannot satisfactorily account, of pecuniary resources, or property
disproportionate to his known sources of income, or that such person, has, on
or about the time of offence with which he is charged, obtained an accretion to
his pecuniary resources or property for which he cannot satisfactorily account,
may be proved, and may be taken into consideration by the Special Judge as a
relevant fact in deciding whether he is guilty of the particular offence with
which he is charged.
(2) Where in any trial before a Special Judge of an
offence punishable under section 161 to 165 of the Indian Penal Code. Act, XLV
of 1860, it is a proved that an accused person has accepted or obtained, or has
agreed to accept or attempted to obtain, for himself or for any other person,
any gratification (other than legal remuneration) or any valuable thing, or any
pecuniary advantage from a person or the agent of a person, for any favour shown or promised to be shown by the accused person,
it shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that he accepted or
obtained, or agreed to accept or attempted to obtain, that gratification, or
that valuable thing or pecuniary advantage to himself or some. other person, as
the case may be, as a motive or reward such as is mentioned in sections 161,
162 and 163 of the Indian Penal Code, or as the case "may be, without
consideration or for a consideration which he knows to be inadequate :
Provided that the Court may decline
to draw such presumption if the gratification or thing or pecuniary advantage
aforesaid is in its opinion so trival that no
inference of corruption may fairly be drawn from the same.

Bar on trial de novo

Act No
Act No. XIX of 1948
Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act,
1948.
An Act to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of certain offences punish Able under the Ionian Penal
Code and cer tain other Laws.
PREAMBLE
Whereas it is
expedient to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of
certain offences punishable under the Indian Penal Code and certain other laws;
It is hereby
enacted as follows;
7. Bar on trial de
novo.-A special Judge, unless he otherwise decides, shall not be bound to
recall or rehear any witness, whose evidence was already been recorded, or to
re-open proceedings already held, but may act on the evidence already produced
or recorded and continue the trial from the stage which the case has reached.

Punishment of offences

Act No
Act No. XIX of 1948
Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act,
1948.
An Act to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of certain offences punish Able under the Ionian Penal
Code and cer tain other Laws.
PREAMBLE
Whereas it is
expedient to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of
certain offences punishable under the Indian Penal Code and certain other laws;
It is hereby
enacted as follows;
8. Punishment of
offences.-When any person charged before a Special Judge with an
offence triable under this Act is found guilty of the
offence, the Special .Judge shall, notwithstanding anything contained in any
other law, whether or not he imposes a sentence of imprisonment, impose a
sentence of fine which shall not be less than the gain found to have been
derived by the accused by the commission of the offence.

Appeal, Revision and Transfer of Cases

Act No
Act No. XIX of 1948
Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act,
1948.
An Act to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of certain offences punish Able under the Ionian Penal
Code and cer tain other Laws.
PREAMBLE
Whereas it is
expedient to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of
certain offences punishable under the Indian Penal Code and certain other laws;
It is hereby
enacted as follows;
9. Appeal,
Revision and Transfer of Cases.-(1)
An appeal from the judgment of a Special Judge shall lie to the highest
Court, having appellate jurisdiction in the territorial limits in which the
offence is tried by the Special Judge, and the same Court shall also have
powers of revision.
(2) The aforesaid Court shall have authority to
transfer any case from the Court of a Special Judge, to the Court of another
Special Judge:
Provided that notwithstanding anything contained in
section 526 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure (Act V of 1898) the Special Judge from whose Court a transfer is
desired, shall not be bound to adjourn the case, but if he rejects a request
for adjournment, he shall record his reasons for doing so.
(3) No prosecution under this Act against any person
either generally or in respect of any one or more of the offences for which he
is being tried shall be withdrawn except under the orders in writing of the
Central Government.

Bail and Imprisonment

Act No
Act No. XIX of 1948
Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act,
1948.
An Act to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of certain offences punish Able under the Ionian Penal
Code and cer tain other Laws.
PREAMBLE
Whereas it is
expedient to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of
certain offences punishable under the Indian Penal Code and certain other laws;
It is hereby
enacted as follows;
10. Bail and
Imprisonment.-(1) Notwithstanding
anything contained in the Second Schedule of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
Act V of 1898, or any other law for the time being in force, offences to be
tried by the Special Judge under the provisions of this Act shall be deemed to
be non--bailable.
(2) Any offence mentioned in the schedule which is
punishable with simple imprisonment shall be deemed to be punishable with
imprisonment of either description.

Powers to make Rules

Act No
Act No. XIX of 1948
Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act,
1948.
An Act to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of certain offences punish Able under the Ionian Penal
Code and cer tain other Laws.

Whereas it is

certain offences punishable under the Indian Penal Code and certain other laws;
It is hereby

11. Powers to
make Rules.-(1) The Central
Government may frame rules to carry out the purposes of this Act.
(2) In particular, and without prejudice to the
generally of the foregoing powers, such rules may provide for any of the
following matters, namely:-
(a) Authorisation of persons to exercise the power to sanction
prosecu tions on behalf of the Central Government in respect of various grades
of public servants;
(b) the emoluments of the Special Judges, and their appointment
;
(c) territorial limits of the jurisdiction of Special Judges and
the place and time sitting of the Courts presided over by the Special Judge ;
(d) the summoning of witnesses and compelling the production of
docu ments and the penalty for disobeying, or evading the same, in addition to 'or substitution of the provisions of the
Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 ;
(e) other matters incidental to the above.

Act No
Act No. XIX of 1948
Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act,
1948.
An Act to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of certain offences punish Able under the Ionian Penal
Code and cer tain other Laws.
PREAMBLE
Whereas it is
expedient to provide for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of
certain offences punishable under the Indian Penal Code and certain other laws;
It is hereby
enacted as follows;
SCHEDULE
(See section 3 of this Act)
(a) Offences punishable under
sections 161 to 166, 168, 217, 218, 379 to 382, 403 to 409, 411, 414, 417 to
420, 465 to 468, 471, 474 and 477A of the Indian Penal code:
(b) offences
punishable under the Prevention of Corruption Act II of 1947;
(c) attempts,
abetments and conspiracies in relation to, or connected with, the offences
mentioned in clauses (a) and (b).
